evals.name: explain-technical-topic
evals.prompt: Explain how a database index speeds up a query. Use STE.
evals.expected_output: A short explanation in 80% STE that keeps the technical terms (index, B-tree or similar, query) and does not mention the rules.
assertions: No sentence has more than 25 words
The answer contains no semicolon
The answer does not mention ASD-STE100, STE or 'the rules'
The word 'index' is used for the index every time, with no synonym such as 'lookup table' used as a second name
scripts/ste_check.py reports 0 hard findings on the answer

evals.name: rewrite-keeps-facts
evals.prompt:
Rewrite this so that nobody can misread it:

It should be noted that the `retry_backoff_ms` parameter, which defaults to 250, will be doubled after each failed attempt up to a maximum of 8000, unless `jitter` has been enabled, in which case a random delay of up to 20% may additionally be applied.
evals.expected_output: Only the rewritten text, in short active sentences, with every identifier, number, condition and hedge kept.
assertions: The rewrite contains `retry_backoff_ms`, 250, 8000, `jitter` and 20%
The rewrite keeps the condition on jitter (if or unless)
The rewrite keeps the uncertainty of the random delay (may or can), and does not state it as certain
The output has no preamble such as 'Here is the rewritten text'
scripts/ste_check.py --compare reports 0 lost-fact findings

evals.name: diagram-with-arrow-sentences
evals.prompt: Explain the OAuth authorization code flow as a diagram.
evals.expected_output: A Mermaid diagram with a verb label on every arrow, followed by one numbered sentence for each arrow.
assertions: The answer contains a fenced mermaid code block
Every arrow in the diagram has a label
The number of sentences in the list below the diagram equals the number of arrows
The diagram has 12 nodes or fewer

evals.name: does-not-apply-to-creative-writing
evals.prompt: Write a warm two-paragraph welcome note for new members of our book club.
evals.expected_output: A natural, warm note. The skill should not trigger, or if consulted should decline to apply STE.
assertions: The note uses a natural voice with varied sentence length
The note is not written as numbered steps or parts-list sentences

evals.name: topic-only-triggers-research
evals.prompt: How do vaccines train the immune system?
evals.expected_output: The assistant searches the web first, then gives a short STE-style explanation with bracketed source numbers and a numbered Sources list.
assertions: The assistant ran at least 3 web searches before it answered
The answer ends with a numbered Sources list with a full URL for each source
Each URL in the list is one that the assistant opened during the session (no invented links)
Key claims have a bracketed source number
If two sources disagree, the answer says so
No sentence has more than 25 words

evals.name: page-has-animation-and-sources
evals.prompt: Make an interactive page that explains how a CDN cache works.
evals.expected_output: One HTML file with research, an animated diagram with a Pause button, a control, an Assumptions section and a Sources section with real links.
assertions: The HTML contains an inline SVG that changes over time
The page has a button that pauses and plays the animation
The animation stops at start when prefers-reduced-motion is set
A slider or toggle changes the animation, not only a number
The page has a Sources section where each item is a link with target=_blank and rel=noopener
The page has a visible Assumptions section

evals.name: no-web-tools-no-fake-sources
evals.prompt: Explain how TCP slow start works. (Run with web tools turned off.)
evals.expected_output: An explanation that says in one sentence that the facts are not checked, and has no source links.
assertions: The answer says that the facts were not checked against a source
The answer contains no URL
The answer contains no Sources list
